_note: Distinct information per queen. Each queen's workers see only their own brief (plus, in the feedback arms, verifier failure text or board notes). The single agent sees all three. Portal homepages only; no dataset-level URLs, so the agents still have to find the dataset.

q-evolution.brief: Portals you know well: GBIF (https://www.gbif.org, occurrence and species APIs with establishmentMeans and island/country fields), IUCN Red List (https://www.iucnredlist.org, native ranges), AmphibiaWeb (https://amphibiaweb.org), FishBase (https://www.fishbase.se, freshwater fish by country and basin), Avibase and eBird (https://ebird.org), the Paleobiology Database (https://paleobiodb.org, fossil occurrences and ages), the International Chronostratigraphic Chart (https://stratigraphy.org/chart), Macrostrat (https://macrostrat.org, stratigraphic units and erosion rates), NCBI (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, genomes and sequence data for domestication ancestry), and GloNAF (naturalised alien floras, https://glonaf.org). For a claim about island faunas prefer an occurrence dataset with island or country fields; for a claim about geological time prefer a chart or database with numeric ages.

q-morphology.brief: Portals you know well: the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey NHANES (https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes, measured stature and weight by age and sex), WHO Child Growth Standards (https://www.who.int/tools/child-growth-standards), ICES DATRAS (https://www.ices.dk/data/data-portals/Pages/DATRAS.aspx, fish length-at-age and weight-length by survey), FishBase (https://www.fishbase.se, length-weight parameters a and b per species), MorphoSource (https://www.morphosource.org, 3D scans of specimens), VertNet and iDigBio (https://vertnet.org, https://www.idigbio.org, museum specimen measurements), the Animal Genome Size and chromosome number resources such as the Chromosome Counts Database CCDB (http://ccdb.tau.ac.il) and the Animal Genome Size Database (https://www.genomesize.com), the International Tree-Ring Data Bank at NOAA NCEI (https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/paleoclimatology/tree-ring), and egg-shape and bird-trait datasets on Dryad. For a claim about human growth prefer a survey with measured, not self-reported, stature.

q-holdout.domain: Data curation: general repositories and collections (no subject specialty)
q-holdout.brief: Portals you know well: Dryad (https://datadryad.org, data behind published papers, searchable by keyword, every dataset has a DOI), Zenodo (https://zenodo.org), figshare (https://figshare.com), PANGAEA (https://www.pangaea.de, earth and environmental data with DOIs), Harvard Dataverse (https://dataverse.harvard.edu), the Natural History Museum Data Portal (https://data.nhm.ac.uk), Smithsonian collections (https://collections.si.edu), Open Tree of Life (https://tree.opentreeoflife.org) and TimeTree (https://timetree.org) for phylogenies, and Wikidata (https://www.wikidata.org) for identifiers. You have no subject specialty: your strength is finding a dataset that has a DOI and a file list, and checking that its landing page exists before you name it.
